title: Unify SDK test harness: deterministic fixtures & VCR contract suite
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a unified, language-agnostic SDK test harness that: 1) Produces deterministic fixtures for Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs (includes streaming events, retry scenarios, and KV-cache/sequence behaviors), 2) Enables VCR-style recording/playback for CI that is resilient to nondeterministic fields, and 3) Runs contract tests against a lightweight mock Redwood API to catch incompatibilities early.

Background: Currently each SDK repo has ad-hoc fixtures and integration tests (some rely on live calls). This creates flaky CI and duplicate effort when recording streaming sessions or simulating partial failures. The product teams are onboarding new streaming features and retries behavior (backoff, idempotency tokens, partial content on disconnect), so we must ensure SDK ergonomics are validated across languages.

Scope: Deliver a reference mock-server + fixture schema, VCR tooling for recording and sanitizing sessions, a set of canonical contract tests (schema/headers/error codes/timing guarantees), and example test suites for Python, TS, and Go that demonstrate deterministic streaming and retry scenarios. Integrate into SDK CI and provide docs for contributors.
acceptance_criteria: A documented fixture schema (JSON Lines or canonical format) that can represent: request metadata, ordered server events (stream frames), injected network faults (delay/drop), and time offsets.
A lightweight mock Redwood API server (Go binary and Node dev server) that can playback fixtures deterministically and expose hooks to inject latency and disconnections.
VCR recorder/playback tool that sanitizes tokens, timestamps, request-ids and produces stable fixtures; language wrappers or example usage in Python/TS/Go.
At least three contract tests that run in CI across all SDKs: schema validation, streaming frame ordering, and retry semantics under transient 5xx failures.
CI gating: failing contract/VCR tests should block releases when SDK surface changes are detected.
Developer docs and a migration guide for existing ad-hoc tests to the new harness.
Examples in each SDK repo demonstrating: streaming response replay, retry backoff simulation, and deterministic prefix-caching behavior for continuation calls.

discussion: 2026-03-02 - Design sync: Decided canonical fixture should be newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) to stream frames; each record has type: request|response_frame|meta|fault. Rationale: streaming-friendly and simple to parse in tests.

2026-03-03 - Trade-off: Full-featured mock with language-specific SDK hooks vs single replay server. We agreed to ship a single replaying server plus thin client helpers in each SDK (less duplication, easier maintenance).

2026-03-04 - PR feedback (GH: redwood/sdktest#182): Add a checksum field to fixtures to detect accidental edits; also suggested 'matchers' section for header/metadata looser comparisons (e.g., Authorization normalized).

2026-03-05 - Streaming ergonomics note: For TS/JS SDK we should expose both event-emitter and async-iterator APIs in examples. For Go, we should demonstrate io.Reader-like streaming and context cancellation semantics.

2026-03-07 - Retry semantics: We will encode idempotency tokens in fixtures and validate that SDK replays with same token on retries. Also record server-side counters to assert deduplication behavior in contract tests.

Links: Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/sdk-fixtures; GH prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdktest-proto; Example CI job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/actions/runs/12345678
implementation_notes: Fixture format v1: fields: time_offset_ms, record_type, method, path, headers, body, frame_index, fault(type, latency_ms, drop_after_n). Represent streaming frames as consecutive response_frame records with frame_index to maintain ordering.
Sanitization rules: redact Authorization, API-Key, request-id; canonicalize timestamps to offsets; normalize hostnames to fixture host placeholder.

Mock server features: deterministic replay, ability to pause between frames by time_offset, simulate TCP reset on a frame, respond with 5xx for Nth request, and expose admin endpoint to load fixtures and view playback state.
VCR tool: should support a 'record --sanitize' mode that saves to fixtures/vcr/YYYYMMDD-name.ndjson. Provide --allowlist for headers that may vary per environment.
Contract assertions: JSON Schema validation of responses, streaming order assertions, and retry idempotency assertion (server side counter checked in playback admin API).

CI integration: run contract tests in matrix for node 18/20, python 3.11, go 1.21 across linux/amd64, and a lightweight macOS runner for streaming behavior parity. Cache fixtures in CI runner artifacts to avoid network flakiness.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fixtures drift when backend changes types/fields. Mitigation: include schema_version in fixtures and fail tests with clear migration steps.
Risk: Recording live traffic may capture PII or secrets. Mitigation: strict sanitizers, manual review step for first recordings, and allowlist-only recordings in CI.
Risk: Contributors find fixture format hard to author. Mitigation: provide a 'fixture authoring' CLI and sample recordings for common flows.

Risk: Mock server divergence from real Redwood behavior. Mitigation: keep minimal surface area for contract tests and periodically run smoke tests against staging Redwood API to validate expectations.
